Okay, let's tackle this query step by step. The user provided a detailed NDA document with span markers and 17 hypotheses. My task is to review each hypothesis against the NDA, determine if it's Entailment, Contradiction, or NotMentioned, and provide evidence spans and reasons. 

Starting with nda-11: "Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information." The NDA doesn't mention reverse engineering specifically. The closest is section 4, which talks about using info only for the Purpose and not disclosing it. But there's no mention of reverse engineering. So this is NotMentioned.

Next, nda-16: "Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement." Section 24 says upon termination, Recipient must return or destroy at Discloser's discretion, except keeping one copy for legal obligations. This matches, so Entailment with span 24.

nda-15: "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information." Section 26 states no rights are granted except as in the License Agreement. So Entailment, span 26.

nda-10: "Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated." The NDA doesn't mention keeping the agreement's existence confidential. So NotMentioned.

nda-2: "Confidential Information shall only include technical information." Section 3 lists Confidential Info as including data, techniques, protocols, results, business, financial, etc. So it's not limited to technical. Contradiction, span 3.

nda-1: "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." Section 3 says it's identified as confidential at disclosure. So Entailment, span 3.

nda-19: "Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement." Section 19 says Section 4 survives termination. Entailment, span 19.

nda-12: "Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information." Section 9 says if developed independently, it's excluded. So Entailment, span 9.

nda-20: "Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information." Section 24 allows keeping one copy for legal purposes. Entailment, span 24.

nda-3: "Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information." Section 3 includes "any information" disclosed, which could be verbal. Entailment, span 3.

nda-18: "Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives." Section 18 mentions not using names in literature without approval, but no direct mention of solicitation. NotMentioned.

nda-7: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors)." Section 18 allows disclosure to Receiving Individuals on need-to-know basis. So Entailment, span 18.

nda-17: "Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances." The NDA doesn't mention copying, but section 24 allows keeping one copy. But the hypothesis is about creating a copy, which isn't directly addressed. NotMentioned.

nda-8: "Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information." Section 11 says they must notify Discloser before disclosure. Entailment, span 11.

nda-13: "Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party." Section 5's exclusion (iii) allows info from third parties with bona fide rights. Entailment, spans 5 and 8.

nda-5: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees." Section 18 allows disclosure to employees on need-to-know. Entailment, span 18.

nda-4: "Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement." Section 16 says they can't use it for other purposes. Entailment, span 16.
